title: In a superconductor, current can flow for years with no power
body: Cool certain materials below a critical temperature and their electrical resistance doesn’t just get small, it drops to exactly zero. A current started in a superconducting loop keeps circulating with no battery: experiments show no measurable decay over years, pointing to lifetimes of at least 100,000 years. Superconductors also push out magnetic fields, which is why a magnet can float above one. MRI scanners rely on superconducting coils for their strong fields.

slides.question: Why can a magnet float above a superconductor?
options: Cold air beneath the magnet lifts it
It pushes magnetic fields out of itself
It attracts the magnet from below
slides.explanation: Superconductors push out magnetic fields, so a magnet above one is held up rather than resting on it. The same materials carry current with exactly zero resistance.
